19·31S6-Q30Stephane set 6 · Q30Design High-Performing Architectures

A company has noticed several provisioned throughput exceptions on its DynamoDB database due to major spikes in the writes to the database. The development team wants to decouple the application layer from the database layer and dedicate a worker process to writing the data to DynamoDB.

Which middleware do you recommend on using that can scale infinitely and meet these requirements?

database-এ write-এর বড় spike-এর কারণে একটি company তার DynamoDB database-এ কয়েকটি provisioned throughput exception লক্ষ্য করেছে। development team application layer-কে database layer থেকে decouple করতে চায় এবং DynamoDB-তে data write করার জন্য একটি worker process নির্দিষ্ট করতে চায়।

কোন middleware ব্যবহার করার recommend করবেন, যা অসীমভাবে scale করতে পারে এবং এই requirement পূরণ করে?

Correct: D. Why it is right

Write spike e provisioned throughput exception. App ar DB er majhe SQS rakho: app queue te message dey, dedicated worker DynamoDB er capacity onujayi likhe (PDF p. 394, "SQS as a buffer to database writes").

SQS infinitely scalable, consume na hoa porjonto message thake, tai write harabe na.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. DAX shudhu read cache kore, write spike er throttle komay na.
  • B. KDS e shard capacity size korte hoy (provisioned mode), 'scale infinitely' na; intended buffer SQS.
  • C. SNS push kore, message persist kore na (deliver na hole lost), tai buffer hisebe chole na.

Keyword: spikes in writes + worker process + scale infinitely → SQS

Original explanation (English)

Correct option:

Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) - Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service that enables you to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. SQS offers two types of message queues. Standard queues offer maximum throughput, best-effort ordering, and at-least-once delivery. SQS FIFO queues are designed to guarantee that messages are processed exactly once, in the exact order that they are sent.

Using SQS as a middleware will help us sustain the write throughput during write peaks and therefore this option is the best fit for the given use-case.

Incorrect options:

DynamoDB DAX - Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for DynamoDB that delivers up to a 10x performance improvement – from milliseconds to microseconds – even at millions of requests per second. DAX does all the heavy lifting required to add in-memory acceleration to your DynamoDB tables, without requiring developers to manage cache invalidation, data population, or cluster management.

DAX is used for caching reads, not to help with writes. So this option is ruled out.

Kinesis Data Streams - Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (KDS) is a massively scalable and durable real-time data streaming service. KDS can continuously capture gigabytes of data per second from hundreds of thousands of sources such as website clickstreams, database event streams, financial transactions, social media feeds, IT logs, and location-tracking events. The throughput of an Amazon Kinesis data stream is designed to scale without limits via increasing the number of shards within a data stream.

Kinesis cannot scale infinitely and we may have the same throughput issues. Therefore this option is not the right fit for the given use-case.

Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) - Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) is a highly available, durable, secure, fully managed pub/sub messaging service that enables you to decouple microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. SNS won't keep our data if it cannot be delivered, so this option is incorrect.

Reference:

https://aws.amazon.com/sqs/

References: https://aws.amazon.com/sqs/

19·32S6-Q32Stephane set 6 · Q32Design High-Performing Architectures

An engineering team wants to orchestrate multiple Amazon ECS task types running on EC2 instances that are part of the ECS cluster. The output and state data for all tasks need to be stored. The amount of data output by each task is approximately 20 MB and there could be hundreds of tasks running at a time. As old outputs are archived, the storage size is not expected to exceed 1 TB.

As a solutions architect, which of the following would you recommend as an optimized solution for high-frequency reading and writing?

একটি engineering team ECS cluster-এর অংশ EC2 instance-এ চলা একাধিক Amazon ECS task type orchestrate করতে চায়। সব task-এর output এবং state data store করতে হবে। প্রতিটি task প্রায় 20 MB data output করে এবং একসাথে শত শত task চলতে পারে। পুরোনো output archive করা হয় বলে storage size 1 TB অতিক্রম করবে বলে আশা করা হয় না।

একজন solutions architect হিসেবে, high-frequency reading ও writing-এর জন্য optimized solution হিসেবে নিচের কোনটি আপনি recommend করবেন?

Correct: A. Why it is right

Onek ECS host theke shared storage lage → EFS. Kintu size 1 TB er kom: Bursting mode e throughput size er sathe bare (1 TB = 50 MiB/s), tai choto FS e throughput kom.

Provisioned Throughput e storage size chara-i throughput set kora jay (PDF p. 115), tai high-frequency read/write er jonno eta. (Course er Elastic mode-o fit korto, kintu option e nai.)

Why the other options are wrong

  • B. Bursting e throughput storage size er upor nirbhor kore; 1 TB er kom data te high-frequency I/O er jonno throughput kom porbe.
  • C. DynamoDB item max 400 KB, 20 MB output rakha jabe na; file storage-o na.
  • D. EBS ek AZ e ek instance e attach (shared na), tai sob ECS instance ek data share korte parbe na.

Keyword: ECS tasks shared storage + < 1 TB + high-frequency read/write → EFS Provisioned Throughput

Original explanation (English)

Correct option:

Amazon EFS file systems are distributed across an unconstrained number of storage servers. This distributed data storage design enables file systems to grow elastically to petabyte scale. It also enables massively parallel access from compute instances, including Amazon EC2, Amazon ECS, and AWS Lambda, to your data.

Use Amazon EFS with Provisioned Throughput mode - Provisioned Throughput mode is available for applications with high throughput to storage (MiB/s per TiB) ratios, or with requirements greater than those allowed by the Bursting Throughput mode. For example, say you're using Amazon EFS for development tools, web serving, or content management applications where the amount of data in your file system is low relative to throughput demands. Your file system can now get the high levels of throughput your applications require without having to pad your file system.

If your file system is in the Provisioned Throughput mode, you can increase the Provisioned Throughput of your file system as often as you want. You can decrease your file system throughput in Provisioned Throughput mode as long as it's been more than 24 hours since the last decrease. Additionally, you can change between Provisioned Throughput mode and the default Bursting Throughput mode as long as it’s been more than 24 hours since the last throughput mode change.

[chobi: original link, ekhon na-o thakte pare] via - https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/performance.html

Incorrect options:

Use Amazon EFS with Bursting Throughput mode - With Bursting Throughput mode, a file system's throughput scales as the amount of data stored in the standard storage class grows. File-based workloads are typically spiky, driving high levels of throughput for short periods of time, and low levels of throughput the rest of the time. To accommodate this, Amazon EFS is designed to burst to high throughput levels for periods of time. By default, AWS recommends that you run your application in the Bursting Throughput mode. But, if you're planning to migrate large amounts of data into your file system, consider switching to Provisioned Throughput mode.

The use-case mentions that the solution should be optimized for high-frequency reading and writing even when the old outputs are archived, therefore Provisioned Throughput mode is a better fit as it guarantees high levels of throughput your applications require without having to pad your file system.

Use an Amazon EBS volume mounted to the ECS cluster instances - EFS has a higher throughput than EBS. In addition, EBS can be attached to multiple EC2 instances when the underlying EBS type is io1/io2 and the instance is of Nitro type. The use-case does not provide any such details, so this option is ruled out.

Use a DynamoDB table that is accessible by all ECS cluster instances - DynamoDB is not a fit for this scenario as each task output is 20 MB but the storage limit for each item in a DynamoDB table is 400 KB. You could write custom code to split the task output data into multiple items but it is not an optimal solution compared to using EFS in Provisioned Throughput mode.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/performance.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Limits.html#limits-items

References: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/performance.html · https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Limits.html#limits-items

19·33S6-Q35Stephane set 6 · Q35Design High-Performing Architectures

A company's real-time streaming application is running on AWS. As the data is ingested, a job runs on the data and takes 30 minutes to complete. The workload frequently experiences high latency due to large amounts of incoming data. A solutions architect needs to design a scalable and serverless solution to enhance performance.

Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take? (Select two)

একটি company-র real-time streaming application AWS-এ চলছে। data ingest হওয়ার সাথে সাথে data-র উপর একটি job চলে এবং সম্পূর্ণ হতে 30 মিনিট লাগে। প্রচুর পরিমাণ incoming data-র কারণে workload প্রায়ই high latency-র সম্মুখীন হয়। performance বাড়াতে একজন solutions architect-কে একটি scalable এবং serverless solution design করতে হবে।

solutions architect-এর কোন step-গুলোর combination নেওয়া উচিত? (2টি বেছে নিন) (Select two)

Choose 2 answers

Correct: C, E. Why it is right

  • Kinesis Data Streams: real-time stream onek data scale kore ingest kore (PDF p. 407).
  • ECS on Fargate: serverless container, 15 min limit nai, tai 30 min er job chalate pare (PDF p. 424).

Duitai scalable + serverless.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. DMS database migration er jonno, streaming data ingest er jonno na.
  • B. Lambda er max 15 min; protita 30 min er job ek Lambda te cholbe na, Step Functions diye-o shei limit thake.
  • D. EC2 ASG serverless na; instance manage korte hoy.

Keyword: real-time streaming + job 30 minutes + serverless → Kinesis Data Streams + Fargate

Original explanation (English)

Correct options:

Set up Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data

Set up AWS Fargate with Amazon ECS to process the data

Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (KDS) is a massively scalable and durable real-time data streaming service. KDS can continuously capture gigabytes of data per second from hundreds of thousands of sources such as website clickstreams, database event streams, financial transactions, social media feeds, IT logs, and location-tracking events. The data collected is available in milliseconds to enable real-time analytics use cases such as real-time dashboards, real-time anomaly detection, dynamic pricing, and more.

AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that works with both Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS). Fargate makes it easy for you to focus on building your applications. Fargate removes the need to provision and manage servers, lets you specify and pay for resources per application, and improves security through application isolation by design.

For the given use case, we can use Kinesis Data Streams as the ingestion layer and the containerized ECS application on AWS Fargate as the processing layer. Both these components are serverless and can scale to offer the desired performance.

Incorrect options:

Set up AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data - AWS Database Migration Service helps you migrate databases to AWS quickly and securely. DMS cannot be used for real-time data ingestion. Hence, this option is incorrect.

Set up AWS Lambda with AWS Step Functions to process the data - The maximum timeout value for any AWS Lambda function is 15 minutes. When the specified timeout is reached, AWS Lambda terminates the execution of your Lambda function. Since the use case talks about a job that runs for 30 minutes, Lambda is not an option here.

Provision EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to process the data - The given requirement is for a serverless solution to process the data. Hence, provisioning an EC2 instance is clearly not the right solution.

Reference:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/big-data/building-a-scalable-streaming-data-processor-with-amazon-kinesis-data-streams-on-aws-fargate/

References: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/big-data/building-a-scalable-streaming-data-processor-with-amazon-kinesis-data-streams-on-aws-fargate/

19·34S6-Q52Stephane set 6 · Q52Design High-Performing Architectures

You are using AWS Lambda to implement a batch job for a big data analytics workflow. Based on historical trends, a similar job runs for 30 minutes on average. The Lambda function pulls data from Amazon S3, processes it, and then writes the results back to S3. When you deployed your AWS Lambda function, you noticed an issue where the Lambda function abruptly failed after 15 minutes of execution.

As a solutions architect, which of the following would you identify as the root cause of the issue?

আপনি একটি big data analytics workflow-এর জন্য একটি batch job implement করতে AWS Lambda ব্যবহার করছেন। historical trend অনুযায়ী, একই রকম একটি job গড়ে 30 মিনিট চলে। Lambda function Amazon S3 থেকে data pull করে, process করে এবং তারপর result আবার S3-এ write করে। আপনি যখন আপনার AWS Lambda function deploy করলেন, তখন একটি সমস্যা লক্ষ্য করলেন যে 15 মিনিট execution-এর পরে Lambda function হঠাৎ fail করেছে।

একজন solutions architect হিসেবে, এই সমস্যার root cause হিসেবে নিচের কোনটি আপনি চিহ্নিত করবেন?

Correct: C. Why it is right

Lambda er max timeout 15 min (900 s) (PDF p. 451). Job average 30 min, tai function exactly 15 min por abruptly fail kore = timeout.

Lomba batch job er jonno EC2/ECS/Fargate use koro.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Memory shesh hole ekta specific 15 min mark e na, jekono shomoy error dito.
  • B. Runtime vul hole function shurutei fail korto.
  • D. Permission na thakle S3 theke data pull kora shurutei fail hoto, 15 min por na.

Keyword: job 30 min, fails after 15 minutes → Lambda timeout

Original explanation (English)

Correct option:

AWS Lambda lets you run code without provisioning or managing servers. You pay only for the compute time you consume.

With Lambda, you can run code for virtually any type of application or backend service - all with zero administration. Just upload your code and Lambda takes care of everything required to run and scale your code with high availability. You can set up your code to automatically trigger from other AWS services or call it directly from any web or mobile app. AWS Lambda functions can be configured to run up to 15 minutes per execution. You can set the timeout to any value between 1 second and 15 minutes.

The AWS Lambda function is timing out - AWS Lambda functions time out after 15 minutes, and are not usually meant for long-running jobs.

Incorrect options:

The AWS Lambda function is running out of memory - Memory errors will not result in the abrupt termination of the function with no error message.

The AWS Lambda function chosen runtime is wrong - Lambda function execution will fail if there is an issue with runtime. So, this is not the issue in the current case.

The AWS Lambda function is missing IAM permissions - Without enough permissions, Lambda would not have been able to start its execution at all. So, permissions are not an issue here.

Reference:

https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/faqs/

References: https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/faqs/

20·1S4-Q44Stephane set 4 · Q44Design Cost-Optimized Architectures

A new REST API you have developed is leveraging the API Gateway, AWS Lambda and an Aurora database. Most of the workload is read heavy to the nature of the website. The data rarely changes and it is acceptable to serve our users outdated data for 24 hours. Recently, the website has been experiencing high load and the costs incurred on the Aurora database have been very high. How can you easily reduce the costs while improving performance, with minimal changes?

আপনার develop করা একটি নতুন REST API, API Gateway, AWS Lambda এবং একটি Aurora database ব্যবহার করছে। website-এর প্রকৃতির কারণে বেশিরভাগ workload read heavy। data কদাচিৎ পরিবর্তন হয় এবং আমাদের user-দের 24 ঘণ্টা পুরোনো (outdated) data serve করা গ্রহণযোগ্য। সম্প্রতি website-এ high load হচ্ছে এবং Aurora database-এ খরচ অনেক বেশি হচ্ছে। সামান্য পরিবর্তনে performance উন্নত করার পাশাপাশি আপনি কীভাবে সহজে খরচ কমাতে পারেন?

Correct: B. Why it is right

Workload read heavy, data kom bodlay, ar stale data cholbe → API Gateway caching. Response API Gateway tei cache hoy, tai repeated request Lambda ar Aurora porjonto jay na → Aurora load ar cost kome, latency o kome.

Eta minimal change: shudhu stage e cache on (MyTodoList "caching at the API Gateway", PDF p. 499). Official doc: TTL max 3600 s, tai 24 h stale allowed er moddhe.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Read replica Aurora er read load nite pare, kintu notun instance mane aro cost; question cost komate bole.
  • C. Lambda er kono native in-memory caching feature nai.
  • D. ALB e switch korle cache hoy na, Aurora er load ar cost ekoi thake.

Keyword: read heavy, rarely changes, outdated data OK + reduce cost, minimal changes → API Gateway caching

Original explanation (English)

Adding Aurora Read Replicas would greatly increase the cost, switching to a Load Balancer would not improve the problems, and AWS Lambda has no native in memory caching capability. Here, using API Gateway Caching feature is the answer, as we can accept to serve stale data to our users.

Related: Section 19 Serverless Overview

20·2S5-Q40Stephane set 5 · Q40Design High-Performing Architectures

A profitable small business has been running their IT systems using the on-premises infrastructure. With growing demand, the business is finding it difficult to manage the IT infrastructure, which is not their core competency. The business plans to move to AWS Cloud, in light of their plans of extending their operations to other countries.

As a Solutions Architect, can you suggest a cost-effective, serverless solution for their flagship application that has both static and dynamic content as part of its core data model?

একটি লাভজনক small business on-premises infrastructure ব্যবহার করে তাদের IT system চালাচ্ছে। চাহিদা বাড়ার সাথে সাথে business-টির পক্ষে IT infrastructure manage করা কঠিন হয়ে পড়ছে, যা তাদের core competency নয়। অন্য দেশে তাদের operations সম্প্রসারণের পরিকল্পনার আলোকে business-টি AWS Cloud-এ যাওয়ার পরিকল্পনা করছে।

একজন Solutions Architect হিসেবে, আপনি কি তাদের flagship application-এর জন্য একটি cost-effective, serverless solution suggest করতে পারেন, যার core data model-এর অংশ হিসেবে static এবং dynamic দুই ধরনের content আছে?

Correct: B. Why it is right

Serverless + static ar dynamic + onek desh = MyBlog.com pattern (PDF p. 501-508):

  • Static content → S3 (sosta).
  • Dynamic content → Lambda + DynamoDB (serverless, infra manage nai).
  • Global → shamne CloudFront, low latency.

Business infra manage korte chay na, tai EC2 / RDS bad.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. S3 shudhu static file serve kore; dynamic content / server-side code chalate pare na.
  • C. EC2 + RDS serverless na; instance manage korte hoy, ja business chay na.
  • D. Static content EC2 theke dewa beshi dami ar kom efficient; ar EC2 + RDS serverless na.

Keyword: serverless + static and dynamic + other countries → S3 + Lambda + DynamoDB + CloudFront

Original explanation (English)

Correct option:

Host the static content on Amazon S3 and use Lambda with DynamoDB for the serverless web application that handles dynamic content. Amazon CloudFront will sit in front of Lambda for distribution across diverse regions - Lambda with DynamoDB is the right answer for a serverless solution. CloudFront will help in enhancing user experience by delivering content, across different geographic locations with low latency. Amazon S3 is a cost-effective and faster way of distributing static content for web applications.

Incorrect options:

Host both the static and dynamic content of the web application on Amazon S3 and use Amazon CloudFront for distribution across diverse regions/countries - S3 is not the right fit for hosting Dynamic content, so this option is incorrect.

Host the static content on Amazon S3 and use Amazon EC2 with RDS for generating the dynamic content. Amazon CloudFront can be configured in front of EC2 instance, to make global distribution easy - The company is looking for a serverless solution, and Amazon EC2 is not a serverless service as the EC2 instances have to be managed by AWS customers.

Host both the static and dynamic content of the web application on Amazon EC2 with RDS as the database. Amazon CloudFront should be configured to distribute the content across geographically disperse regions - This is a possible solution, but not a cost-effective or optimal one. Since static content can be cost-effectively managed on Amazon S3 and can be accessed and distributed faster when compared to fetching the content from the EC2 server.

Reference:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/deliver-your-apps-dynamic-content-using-amazon-cloudfront-getting-started-template/

References: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/deliver-your-apps-dynamic-content-using-amazon-cloudfront-getting-started-template/

21·1S3-Q32Stephane set 3 · Q32Design High-Performing Architectures

A media streaming company is looking to migrate its on-premises infrastructure into the AWS Cloud. The engineering team is looking for a fully managed NoSQL database solution with in-memory caching to maintain low latency that is critical for real-time scenarios such as video streaming and interactive content. The team expects the number of concurrent users to touch up to a million so the database should be able to scale elastically. As a solutions architect, which of the following AWS services would you recommend for this use-case?

একটি media streaming company তাদের on-premises infrastructure AWS Cloud-এ migrate করতে চাইছে। engineering team in-memory caching-সহ একটি fully managed NoSQL database solution খুঁজছে, যাতে low latency বজায় থাকে, যা video streaming ও interactive content-এর মতো real-time scenario-র জন্য অত্যন্ত জরুরি। team আশা করছে concurrent user-এর সংখ্যা এক million পর্যন্ত পৌঁছাতে পারে, তাই database-কে elastically scale করতে পারতে হবে। একজন solutions architect হিসেবে, এই use-case-এর জন্য নিচের কোন AWS service আপনি recommend করবেন?

Correct: A. Why it is right

DynamoDB fully managed serverless NoSQL, elastically scale kore (on-demand / auto scaling). DAX diye built-in in-memory cache, microsecond read latency (PDF p. 522).

Tai "fully managed NoSQL + in-memory caching + million concurrent user" er ek-matro full match DynamoDB (+ DAX).

Why the other options are wrong

  • B. DocumentDB fully managed NoSQL (MongoDB), kintu er nijer in-memory caching layer nai.
  • C. ElastiCache cache layer, fully managed primary NoSQL database na; app code change o lage.
  • D. RDS relational (SQL) database, NoSQL na.

Keyword: fully managed NoSQL + in-memory caching + scale elastically → DynamoDB (+ DAX)

Original explanation (English)

Correct option: "DynamoDB"

Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value and document database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. It's a fully managed, multi-region, multi-master, durable database with built-in security, backup and restore, and in-memory caching for internet-scale applications. DAX is a DynamoDB-compatible caching service that enables you to benefit from fast in-memory performance for demanding applications. Companies use caching through DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) when they have high read volumes or need submillisecond read latency.

Incorrect options: "DocumentDB" - Amazon DocumentDB is a fast, scalable, highly available, and fully managed document database service that supports MongoDB workloads. As a document database, Amazon DocumentDB makes it easy to store, query, and index JSON data. Although DocumentDB is fully managed, it does not have an in-memory caching layer.

"ElastiCache" - Amazon ElastiCache allows you to set up popular open-Source compatible in-memory data stores in the cloud. You can build data-intensive apps or boost the performance of your existing databases by retrieving data from high throughput and low latency in-memory data stores such as Redis and Memcached. Elasticache is used as a caching layer. It's not a fully managed NoSQL database.

"RDS" - RDS makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale a relational database in the cloud. It provides cost-efficient and resizable capacity while automating time-consuming administration tasks such as hardware provisioning, database setup, patching, and backups. It's not a NoSQL database.

References: https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/

References: https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/

21·2S4-Q11Stephane set 4 · Q11Design Resilient Architectures

As a Solutions Architect, you plan on creating a social media website where users can be friends with each other, and like each other's posts. You plan on performing some complicated queries such as "What are the number of likes on the posts that have been posted by the friends of Mike?". What database do you suggest?

একজন Solutions Architect হিসেবে আপনি একটি social media website তৈরির পরিকল্পনা করছেন, যেখানে user-রা একে অপরের friend হতে পারবে এবং একে অপরের post like করতে পারবে। আপনি কিছু জটিল query চালানোর পরিকল্পনা করছেন, যেমন "What are the number of likes on the posts that have been posted by the friends of Mike?"। আপনি কোন database suggest করবেন?

Renamed: Elasticsearch Service -> Amazon OpenSearch Service (the answer is the same).

Correct: A. Why it is right

Friends ar likes er moto highly connected data ar "friends of Mike er post e likes" query = graph traversal. Neptune graph DB, social network, knowledge graph, recommendation er jonno optimized (PDF p. 525).

Why the other options are wrong

  • B. Redshift data warehouse (OLAP analytics / BI), relationship traverse er jonno na.
  • C. ElasticSearch (ekhon Amazon OpenSearch Service) free text search er jonno, graph query er jonno na.
  • D. Aurora relational; join diye kora jay kintu onek hop er relationship query complex ar slow, graph DB best.

Keyword: social media, friends, likes, complicated relationship query → Neptune

Original explanation (English)

Here, we need a graph database due to the highly connected datasets and queries, therefore Neptune is our best answer

Related: Section 22 Data & Analytics · Section 09 RDS + Aurora + ElastiCache

21·3S6-Q17Stephane set 6 · Q17Design Resilient Architectures

The engineering team at an IT company is deploying an Online Transactional Processing (OLTP) application, which will have unpredictable spikes of usage, that they do not know in advance.

Which database would you recommend using?

একটি IT company-র engineering team একটি Online Transactional Processing (OLTP) application deploy করছে, যার usage-এ অনুমান-অযোগ্য spike হবে, যা তারা আগে থেকে জানে না।

আপনি কোন database ব্যবহারের recommend করবেন?

Correct: A. Why it is right

OLTP = relational database er kaaj (RDS / Aurora). "Unpredictable spike, age theke jani na" → Aurora Serverless: unpredictable / intermittent workload, capacity planning nai, nije scale kore (PDF p. 520).

DynamoDB on-demand o spike handle kore, kintu NoSQL, relational OLTP na; tai eta course er intended answer.

Why the other options are wrong

  • B. ElastiCache cache layer, primary OLTP database na, SQL / relational query nai.
  • C. DynamoDB NoSQL; tachara provisioned + auto scaling dhire bara workload er jonno, hothat unpredictable spike er jonno na.
  • D. On-demand spike handle kore thik, kintu DynamoDB NoSQL, relational OLTP er jonno course eta bad dey.

Keyword: OLTP + unpredictable spikes → Aurora Serverless

Original explanation (English)

Correct option:

Aurora Serverless

Amazon Aurora Serverless is an on-demand, auto-scaling configuration for Amazon Aurora (MySQL-compatible and PostgreSQL-compatible editions), where the database will automatically start up, shut down, and scale capacity up or down based on your application's needs. It enables you to run your database in the cloud without managing any database instances. It's a simple, cost-effective option for infrequent, intermittent, or unpredictable workloads. The database design for an OLTP application fits the relational model, therefore you can infer an OLTP system as a Relational Database.

Aurora Serverless is the perfect way to create a database that can scale down to 0 servers, and scale up to many servers, as an OLTP database. So this is the correct option.

Incorrect options:

DynamoDB with Provisioned Capacity and Auto Scaling

DynamoDB with On-Demand Capacity

Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value and document database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. It's a fully managed, multi-region, multi-master, durable database with built-in security, backup and restore, and in-memory caching for internet-scale applications.

DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and doesn't do relational queries, therefore it's a choice we have to eliminate, even though the two modes proposed here help us cope with an unpredictable amount of usage. So both these options are incorrect.

Amazon ElastiCache - Amazon ElastiCache allows you to seamlessly set up, run, and scale popular open-Source compatible in-memory data stores in the cloud. Build data-intensive apps or boost the performance of your existing databases by retrieving data from high throughput and low latency in-memory data stores. Amazon ElastiCache is a popular choice for real-time use cases like Caching, Session Stores, Gaming, Geospatial Services, Real-Time Analytics, and Queuing. Elasticache is used as a caching layer in front of relational databases. ElastiCache is a NoSQL database and doesn't facilitate relational queries, so this option is ruled out.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora/serverless/

https://aws.amazon.com/rds/

References: https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora/serverless/ · https://aws.amazon.com/rds/

22·1S1-Q8Stephane set 1 · Q8Design High-Performing Architectures

An IT company has built a custom data warehousing solution for a retail organization by using Amazon Redshift. As part of the cost optimizations, the company wants to move any historical data (any data older than a year) into S3, as the daily analytical reports consume data for just the last one year. However the analysts want to retain the ability to cross reference this historical data with the daily reports with the least amount of effort and minimum cost. As a solutions architect, which option would you recommend to facilitate this use-case?

একটি IT company Amazon Redshift ব্যবহার করে একটি retail organization-এর জন্য একটি custom data warehousing solution তৈরি করেছে। cost optimization-এর অংশ হিসেবে company যেকোনো historical data (এক বছরের বেশি পুরোনো যেকোনো data) S3-এ সরাতে চায়, কারণ দৈনিক analytical report শুধু গত এক বছরের data ব্যবহার করে। তবে analyst-রা সবচেয়ে কম effort (least amount of effort) ও সর্বনিম্ন cost-এ এই historical data-কে দৈনিক report-এর সাথে cross reference করার সক্ষমতা রাখতে চান। একজন solutions architect হিসেবে, এই use-case সহজ করতে আপনি কোন option recommend করবেন?

Correct: C. Why it is right

Redshift Spectrum diye S3 e rakha data load na kore Redshift theke query kora jay; Redshift cluster query ta hajar hajar Spectrum node e pathay (PDF p. 538).

Tai historical data S3 e soriye Redshift storage cost komao, ar analyst ek-i Redshift query te S3 er historical table ar Redshift er daily data join / cross-reference korte pare: least effort + minimum cost.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Athena alada query korbe, Redshift er daily report alada; cross-reference er jonno flat file export kore abar analysis = beshi effort, cumbersome.
  • B. COPY diye historical data abar Redshift e load korle storage / load cost firey ashe; protibar ad-hoc er jonno load-delete jhamela.
  • D. Glue ETL diye Redshift e load-o ek-i somossa: cost + effort; Spectrum load chara-i query kore.

Keyword: historical data S3 e + cross reference with Redshift reports + least effort / cost → Redshift Spectrum

Original explanation (English)

Amazon Redshift is a fully-managed petabyte-scale cloud based data warehouse product designed for large scale data set storage and analysis.

Using Amazon Redshift Spectrum, you can efficiently query and retrieve structured and semistructured data from files in Amazon S3 without having to load the data into Amazon Redshift tables. Amazon Redshift Spectrum resides on dedicated Amazon Redshift servers that are independent of your cluster. Redshift Spectrum pushes many compute-intensive tasks, such as predicate filtering and aggregation, down to the Redshift Spectrum layer. Thus, Redshift Spectrum queries use much less of your cluster's processing capacity than other queries.

Amazon Athena is an interactive query service that makes it easy to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. Athena is serverless, so there is no infrastructure to setup or manage, and customers pay only for the queries they run. You can use Athena to process logs, perform ad-hoc analysis, and run interactive queries.

Providing access to historical data via Athena would mean that historical data reconciliation would become difficult as the daily report would still be produced via Redshift. Such a setup is cumbersome to maintain on a day to day basis. Hence the option to use Athena is ruled out.

Loading historical data into Redshift via COPY command or Glue ETL job would be cost heavy for a one time ad-hoc process. The same result can be achieved more cost efficiently by using Redshift Spectrum. Therefore both options to load historical data into Redshift are also incorrect for the given use-case.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/c-using-spectrum.html#c-spectrum-overview

References: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/c-using-spectrum.html#c-spectrum-overview

22·2S1-Q11Stephane set 1 · Q11Design Resilient Architecturesnot in course

The traffic monitoring authorities at a city want to monitor the traffic at busy intersections and take corrective action at the earliest. An ML solutions company has developed a Proof-of-Concept for processing this video data and now it wants to productionalize it to cover all city intersections. What is the recommended solution stack with the LEAST amount of development effort and ongoing maintenance?

একটি শহরের traffic monitoring কর্তৃপক্ষ ব্যস্ত intersection-গুলোর traffic monitor করতে এবং যত দ্রুত সম্ভব সংশোধনমূলক ব্যবস্থা নিতে চায়। একটি ML solutions company এই video data process করার জন্য একটি Proof-of-Concept তৈরি করেছে এবং এখন শহরের সব intersection cover করতে এটিকে production-এ নিতে চায়। সবচেয়ে কম development effort ও ongoing maintenance (LEAST amount of development effort and ongoing maintenance)-সহ recommended solution stack কোনটি?

Renamed: Kinesis Data Analytics -> Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (the answer is the same).
Not in the course: Kinesis Video Streams course e poray na (Kinesis section e shudhu Data Streams ar Data Firehose). Mone rakho: live video stream ingest + analysis = Kinesis Video Streams.

Correct: C. Why it is right

Kinesis Video Streams fully managed: device theke live video AWS e stream + durably store kore, tarpor downstream app real-time video processing kore. Managed hoyay development + maintenance kom.

Kinesis Video Streams course e porano hoy nai; mone rakho: live video ingest + analysis = Kinesis Video Streams.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. EMR e Spark Streaming cluster nije manage / tune korte hobe; "least development effort and maintenance" bhange.
  • B. Kinesis Data Streams raw video feed er jonno banano na; protita stream e Lambda + frame analysis nije likhte hobe, onek kaaj.
  • D. Kinesis Data Analytics (ekhon Managed Service for Apache Flink) raw video directly consume korte pare na; KDS / MSK er record stream analyze kore.

Keyword: video data + LEAST development effort and maintenance → Kinesis Video Streams

Original explanation (English)

Amazon Elastic MapReduce (Amazon EMR) is a web service that makes it easy to quickly and cost-effectively process vast amounts of data. Amazon EMR uses Hadoop, an open source framework, to distribute your data and processing across a resizable cluster of Amazon EC2 instances. Using an EMR cluster would imply managing the underlying infrastructure so it’s ruled out because the correct solution for the given use-case should require the least amount of development effort and ongoing maintenance.

Kinesis Data Streams can be used to collect log and event data from sources such as servers, desktops, and mobile devices. Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics is the easiest way to analyze streaming data in real time. Kinesis Data Analytics enables you to easily and quickly build queries and sophisticated streaming applications in three simple steps: setup your streaming data sources, write your queries or streaming applications, and setup your destination for processed data. Kinesis Data Stream and Kinesis Data Analytics cannot directly consume the incoming video feed so these options are incorrect for the given problem statement.

Amazon Kinesis Video Streams is a fully managed AWS service that enables you to stream live video from devices to the AWS Cloud and durably store it. You can then build your own applications for real-time video processing or perform batch-oriented video analytics. Kinesis Video Streams is the correct option as it is fully managed by AWS and therefore it reduces the development and maintenance effort.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesisvideostreams/latest/dg/what-is-kinesis-video.html

References: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesisvideostreams/latest/dg/what-is-kinesis-video.html

Related: Section 17 SQS, SNS, Kinesis, Amazon MQ

22·3S1-Q12Stephane set 1 · Q12Design Cost-Optimized Architectures

The data engineering team at an ecommerce company has set up a workflow to ingest the clickstream data into the raw zone of the S3 data lake. The team wants to run some SQL based data sanity checks on the raw zone of the data lake. What AWS services would you recommend for this use-case such that the solution is cost-effective and easy to maintain?

একটি ecommerce company-র data engineering team S3 data lake-এর raw zone-এ clickstream data ingest করার জন্য একটি workflow set up করেছে। team data lake-এর raw zone-এ কিছু SQL-ভিত্তিক data sanity check চালাতে চায়। এই use-case-এর জন্য আপনি কোন AWS service-গুলো recommend করবেন, যাতে solution cost-effective এবং maintain করা সহজ হয়?

Correct: D. Why it is right

Glue Crawler raw zone er data er schema ekbar pore Glue Data Catalog e table hisabe lekhe (PDF p. 550). Tarpor Athena ei catalog use kore S3 er data te directly SQL chalay, serverless, shudhu scan er taka (PDF p. 531).

Kono data load, cluster ba server nai: cost-effective + easy to maintain.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Hourly Redshift e load korte cluster + load job lage; ekta sanity check er jonno beshi cost ar maintenance.
  • B. RDS e hourly load mane migration job (Lambda / EC2) likhte hobe; RDS boro analytics er jonno o na.
  • C. EMR Spark cluster chalano + hourly load = cluster management ar cost; easy to maintain na.

Keyword: SQL sanity checks on S3 raw zone + cost-effective, easy to maintain → Glue Crawler + Data Catalog + Athena

Original explanation (English)

Amazon Redshift is a fully-managed petabyte-scale cloud based data warehouse product designed for large scale data set storage and analysis. As the development team would have to maintain and monitor the Redshift cluster size and would require significant development time to set up the processes to consume the data on a periodic basis, so this option is ruled out.

Amazon Elastic MapReduce (Amazon EMR) is a web service that makes it easy to quickly and cost-effectively process vast amounts of data. Amazon EMR uses Hadoop, an open source framework, to distribute your data and processing across a resizable cluster of Amazon EC2 instances. Using an EMR cluster would imply managing the underlying infrastructure so it’s ruled out because the correct solution for the given use-case should require the least amount of development effort and ongoing maintenance.

Similarly loading the incremental data into RDS implies data migration jobs will have to be written via a Lambda function or an EC2 based process. This goes against the requirement specified in the use-case.

The best option to use a Glue Crawler to read the raw zone data into a Glue Catalog as a one-time process and then use Athena to run the SQL based sanity checks. Glue Crawler can read raw data schema directly from the source and is serverless, cost-effective and easier to maintain.

22·4S1-Q13Stephane set 1 · Q13Design Cost-Optimized Architectures⚠ outdated

A geological research agency maintains the seismological data for the last 100 years. The data has a velocity of 1GB per minute. You would like to store the data with only the most relevant attributes in order to build a predictive model for earthquakes. What AWS services would you use to build the most cost-effective solution with the LEAST amount of infrastructure maintenance?

একটি geological research agency গত 100 বছরের seismological data রাখে। data-র velocity প্রতি মিনিটে 1GB। ভূমিকম্পের জন্য একটি predictive model তৈরি করতে আপনি শুধু সবচেয়ে প্রাসঙ্গিক attribute-সহ data store করতে চান। সবচেয়ে কম infrastructure maintenance (LEAST amount of infrastructure maintenance)-সহ সবচেয়ে cost-effective (most cost-effective) solution তৈরি করতে আপনি কোন AWS service ব্যবহার করবেন?

⚠ Outdated: Option B er 'Kinesis Data Analytics + SQL queries' (KDA for SQL Applications) discontinued: Oct 15, 2025 theke notun app banano jay na, Jan 27, 2026 theke app delete. Ekhon Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (ba Flink Studio) use korte hoy. Answer (Firehose + Lambda) ekhono thik. source
Renamed: Kinesis Data Firehose -> Amazon Data Firehose; Kinesis Data Analytics -> Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (the answer is the same).

Correct: A. Why it is right

Firehose serverless, auto scale kore, data S3 e deliver kore; sathe Lambda lagiye incoming record filter / transform kora jay (PDF p. 562). Tai shudhu dorkari attribute S3 e jay: storage kom, infrastructure maintenance nai.

Option B er "Kinesis Data Analytics + SQL" (KDA for SQL applications) ekhon discontinued (15 Oct 2025 theke notun app na, 27 Jan 2026 theke delete); answer Firehose + Lambda ekhono thik.

Why the other options are wrong

  • B. Kinesis Data Analytics source theke sorasori ingest kore na (Data Stream / Firehose lage); ar KDA for SQL ekhon discontinued.
  • C. Glue job batch ETL er jonno; 1 GB / minute er continuous stream er near real-time processing er fit na.
  • D. EMR e Spark Streaming cluster manage korte hoy; LEAST infrastructure maintenance bhange.

Keyword: stream e only relevant attributes store + LEAST infrastructure maintenance → Firehose + Lambda → S3

Original explanation (English)

Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics is the easiest way to analyze streaming data in real time. Kinesis Data Analytics enables you to easily and quickly build queries and sophisticated streaming applications in three simple steps: setup your streaming data sources, write your queries or streaming applications, and setup your destination for processed data. Kinesis Data Analytics cannot directly ingest data from the source as it ingests data either from Kinesis Data Streams or Kinesis Data Firehose, so this option is ruled out.

AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, and load (ETL) service that makes it easy for customers to prepare and load their data for analytics. AWS Glue job is meant to be used for batch ETL data processing and it's not the right fit for a near real-time data processing use-case.

Amazon Elastic MapReduce (Amazon EMR) is a web service that makes it easy to quickly and cost-effectively process vast amounts of data. Amazon EMR uses Hadoop, an open source framework, to distribute your data and processing across a resizable cluster of Amazon EC2 instances. Using an EMR cluster would imply managing the underlying infrastructure so it’s ruled out because the correct solution for the given use-case should require the least amount of infrastructure maintenance.

The correct choice is to ingest the data in Kinesis Data Firehose and use a Lambda function to filter and transform the incoming data before the output is dumped on S3. This way you only store a sliced version of the data with only the relevant data attributes required for your model. Also it should be noted that this solution is entirely serverless and requires no infrastructure maintenance.

Related: Section 17 SQS, SNS, Kinesis, Amazon MQ · Section 19 Serverless Overview

22·5S2-Q34Stephane set 2 · Q34Design High-Performing Architectures

A big data consulting firm needs to set up a data lake on Amazon S3 for a HealthCare client. The data lake is split in raw and refined zones. For compliance reasons, the source data needs to be kept for a minimum of 5 years. The source data arrives in the raw zone and is then processed via an AWS Glue based ETL job into the refined zone. The business analysts run ad-hoc queries only on the data in the refined zone using AWS Athena. The team is concerned about the cost of data storage in both the raw and refined zones as the data is increasing at a rate of 1TB on a daily basis in each zone. As a solutions architect, which of the following would you recommend as the MOST cost optimal solution? (Select 2)

একটি big data consulting firm-কে একটি HealthCare client-এর জন্য Amazon S3-এ একটি data lake set up করতে হবে। data lake raw ও refined zone-এ ভাগ করা। compliance-এর কারণে source data অন্তত 5 বছর রাখতে হবে। source data raw zone-এ আসে এবং তারপর একটি AWS Glue-ভিত্তিক ETL job-এর মাধ্যমে process হয়ে refined zone-এ যায়। business analyst-রা AWS Athena ব্যবহার করে শুধু refined zone-এর data-র ওপর ad-hoc query চালান। raw ও refined দুই zone-এই data storage-এর cost নিয়ে team চিন্তিত, কারণ প্রতিটি zone-এ প্রতিদিন 1TB হারে data বাড়ছে। একজন solutions architect হিসেবে, সবচেয়ে cost optimal (MOST cost optimal) solution হিসেবে নিচের কোনগুলো আপনি recommend করবেন? (2টি বেছে নিন) (Select 2)

Choose 2 answers

Correct: A, E. Why it is right

  • Raw zone → Glacier Deep Archive (1 din por): compliance er jonno 5 bochor rakhte hobe, kintu analyst raw zone query kore na; tai sobcheye sosta archive class (lifecycle policy, Section 13).
  • Refined zone compressed format e: Athena eta query kore, tai S3 e-i thakbe; Glue job compressed (columnar hole aro bhalo) format e likhle storage kome ar Athena kom data scan kore (PDF p. 532).

Why the other options are wrong

  • B. Raw data 1 din por delete korle 5 bochor rakhar compliance requirement bhange.
  • C. Refined zone Athena ad-hoc query kore; Deep Archive e gele restore chara query kora jay na.
  • D. CSV uncompressed, row based: storage beshi ar Athena beshi scan kore, cost bare.

Keyword: keep source 5 years (not queried) + Athena queries refined zone + MOST cost optimal → raw: Deep Archive, refined: compressed format

Original explanation (English)

The raw zone consists of the source data, so it cannot be deleted due to compliance reasons. Therefore, we should use a lifecycle policy to transition the raw zone data into Glacier Deep Archive after 1 day of object creation.

We cannot transition the refined zone data into Glacier Deep Archive because it is used by the business analysts for ad-hoc querying. Therefore, the best optimization is to have the refined zone data stored in a compressed format via the Glue job. The compressed data would reduce the storage cost incurred on the data in the refined zone.

Related: Section 12 Amazon S3 Introduction · Section 19 Serverless Overview

22·6S3-Q33Stephane set 3 · Q33Design Resilient Architectures

A big data consulting firm needs to set up a data lake on Amazon S3 for a retail client. The data lake is split in raw and refined zones. The source data arrives in the raw zone and is then processed via an AWS Glue based ETL job into the refined zone. The workflow also involves multiple lambda functions that perform data hygiene and data completeness checks in both the raw and refined zones. The firm is looking for an orchestration solution to manage this end to end workflow. As a solutions architect, which of the following AWS services involves the LEAST development effort for this use-case?

একটি big data consulting firm-কে একটি retail client-এর জন্য Amazon S3-এ একটি data lake set up করতে হবে। data lake raw ও refined zone-এ ভাগ করা। source data raw zone-এ আসে এবং তারপর একটি AWS Glue-ভিত্তিক ETL job-এর মাধ্যমে process হয়ে refined zone-এ যায়। workflow-এ একাধিক lambda function-ও আছে, যেগুলো raw ও refined দুই zone-এই data hygiene ও data completeness check করে। firm এই end to end workflow manage করতে একটি orchestration solution খুঁজছে। একজন solutions architect হিসেবে, এই use-case-এর জন্য নিচের কোন AWS service-এ সবচেয়ে কম development effort (LEAST development effort) লাগে?

Correct: C. Why it is right

Step Functions serverless workflow: Glue ETL job ar onek Lambda function ke order e chalay, protita step track kore, error e retry kore. Glue + Lambda er sathe native integration ache, tai least development effort (Section 19).

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. AWS Batch EC2 te batch compute job chalay; Glue + Lambda er end-to-end orchestration er jonno banano na.
  • B. SWF (course e nai) e workflow er decider logic nije code korte hoy; Step Functions er cheye beshi development effort.
  • D. EMR big data processing cluster; workflow orchestration service na.

Keyword: orchestrate Glue job + Lambda functions + LEAST development effort → Step Functions

Original explanation (English)

Correct option: "AWS Step Functions"

AWS Step Functions lets you coordinate and orchestrate multiple AWS services such as AWS Lambda and AWS Glue into serverless workflows. Workflows are made up of a series of steps, with the output of one step acting as input into the next. A Step Function automatically triggers and tracks each step, and retries when there are errors, so your application executes in order and as expected. The Step Function can ensure that the Glue ETL job and the lambda functions execute in order and complete successfully as per the workflow defined in the given use-case. Therefore, Step Function is the best solution.

How Step Functions Work via - https://aws.amazon.com/step-functions/

Incorrect options: "AWS Batch" - AWS Batch is a set of batch management capabilities that enables developers, scientists, and engineers to easily and efficiently run hundreds of thousands of batch computing jobs on AWS. AWS Batch dynamically provisions the optimal quantity and type of compute resources (e.g., CPU or memory optimized instances) based on the volume and specific resource requirements of the batch jobs submitted. AWS Batch cannot be used to orchestrate a workflow, hence it is an incorrect option.

"Amazon Simple Workflow Service (SWF)" - Amazon SWF helps developers build, run, and scale background jobs that have parallel or sequential steps. In Amazon SWF, tasks represent invocations of logical steps in applications. Tasks are processed by workers which are programs that interact with Amazon SWF to get tasks, process them, and return their results. To coordinate the application execution across workers, you write a program called the decider in your choice of programming language. Although Amazon SWF provides you complete control over your orchestration logic, it increases the complexity of developing applications. Hence this option is not correct.

Exam Alert: Please understand the differences between Amazon SWF vs. AWS Step Functions

via - https://aws.amazon.com/swf/faqs/

"Amazon EMR" - Amazon EMR is the industry-leading cloud big data platform for processing vast amounts of data using open source tools such as Apache Spark, Apache Hive, Apache HBase, Apache Flink, Apache Hudi, and Presto. Amazon EMR uses Hadoop, an open source framework, to distribute your data and processing across a resizable cluster of Amazon EC2 instances. EMR cannot be used to orchestrate a workflow, hence it is an incorrect option.

References: https://aws.amazon.com/step-functions/ https://aws.amazon.com/swf/faqs/

References: https://aws.amazon.com/step-functions/ · https://aws.amazon.com/swf/faqs/

Related: Section 30 Other Services

You have a daily job running on top of your RDS database, running at 7 am. It processes shipping orders for the past day, and usually you get around 2000 rows that need to be processed sequentially in one batch based on a Python script. The processing of each row takes about 3 seconds. What platform do you recommend to run this batch job?

আপনার RDS database-এর ওপর একটি দৈনিক job চলে, যা 7 am-এ চলে। এটি আগের দিনের shipping order process করে, এবং সাধারণত প্রায় 2000টি row পাওয়া যায়, যেগুলো একটি Python script-এর ভিত্তিতে একটি batch-এ sequentially process করতে হয়। প্রতিটি row process করতে প্রায় 3 সেকেন্ড লাগে। এই batch job চালাতে আপনি কোন platform recommend করবেন?

⚠ Outdated: Explanation bole Glue custom Python script chalate pare na - eta ekhon thik na: Glue Python shell job custom Python script chalay (timeout onek ghonta). Tai Glue o kaj korbe, kintu exam/course answer EC2 (Lambda 15 min limit er karone). source

Correct: E. Why it is right

2000 row × 3 s = 6000 s = 100 minute, sequential, ek batch e. Lambda max 15 minute e timeout hobe, tai EC2 e Python script chalano course er answer.

Aaj: original explanation bole Glue custom Python script chalate pare na, eta ar thik na; Glue Python shell job custom Python script chalay (onek ghonta timeout), tai Glue o kaaj korto. Exam / course answer tobuo EC2.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Course er answer e Glue ETL er jonno dhora hoy; aaj Glue Python shell job eta chalate parto, kintu proshner key EC2.
  • B. RDS database; SQL query chalay, Python batch script er compute platform na.
  • C. Lambda max 15 minute; 100 minute er sequential job timeout hobe.
  • D. Kinesis Data Streams real-time streaming er jonno; daily batch job chalay na.

Keyword: 2000 rows × 3 s, sequential, one batch (100 min > Lambda 15 min) → EC2

Original explanation (English)

Lambda would time out after 15 minutes (2000*3=6000 seconds = 100 minutes). Glue is for performing ETL, but cannot run custom Python scripts. Kinesis Streams is for real time data (here we are in a batch setup), RDS could be used to run SQL queries on the data, but no Python script. The correct answer is EC2

22·8S4-Q56Stephane set 4 · Q56Design Cost-Optimized Architectures

Your company has created a data warehouse using Redshift that is used to analyze data from S3. From the usage pattern, you have detected that after 30 days, the data is rarely queried in Redshift and it's not "hot data" anymore. You would like to preserve the SQL querying capability on your data and gets the queries started immediately but adopt a pricing model allowing you to save the maximum amount of cost on Redshift. What do you recommend? (select two)

আপনার company Redshift ব্যবহার করে একটি data warehouse তৈরি করেছে, যা S3-এর data analyze করতে ব্যবহৃত হয়। usage pattern থেকে আপনি দেখেছেন যে 30 দিন পরে Redshift-এ data খুব কমই query করা হয় এবং এটি আর "hot data" নয়। আপনি আপনার data-র ওপর SQL querying capability রাখতে চান এবং query সাথে সাথে শুরু হোক তা চান, কিন্তু এমন একটি pricing model গ্রহণ করতে চান যা আপনাকে Redshift-এ সর্বোচ্চ পরিমাণ cost বাঁচাতে দেয়। আপনি কী recommend করবেন? (2টি বেছে নিন) (select two)

Choose 2 answers

Renamed: S3 Glacier -> S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval (the answer is the same).

Correct: D, E. Why it is right

  • 30 din por data S3 Standard-IA te: kom access hoy kintu dorkar hole sathe sathe pora jay; storage sosta.
  • Athena diye cold data analyze: S3 e directly serverless SQL, query shathe shathe shuru, shudhu scan er taka (PDF p. 531).

Ei bhabe Redshift e shudhu hot data, cost kome, SQL capability thake.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Redshift er internal storage e S3 er moto storage class / tier nai; "S3 IA te migrate" option nai.
  • B. Choto cluster o cluster er taka; data barle storage cost bartei thakbe, maximum saving na.
  • C. Glacier (ekhon Glacier Flexible Retrieval) e query er age restore lage; "queries started immediately" bhange.

Keyword: rarely queried after 30 days + SQL, start immediately + max cost saving → S3 IA + Athena

Original explanation (English)

Creating a smaller cluster with the cold data would not decrease the storage cost of Redshift, which will increase as we keep on creating data. Moving the data to S3 glacier will prevent us from being able to query it. Redshift's internal storage does not have "tiers". Therefore, we should migrate the data to S3 IA and use Athena (serverless SQL query engine on top of S3) to analyze the cold data.

Related: Section 13 Advanced Amazon S3

22·9S4-Q58Stephane set 4 · Q58Design High-Performing Architectures

You would like to perform a daily big data analysis leveraging a Spark job you have written for that purpose. The big data analysis should read the data from S3 and output it back into S3, to be sent back to your customers. Which technology do you recommend to run the Big Data analysis?

আপনি এই উদ্দেশ্যে লেখা একটি Spark job ব্যবহার করে একটি দৈনিক big data analysis করতে চান। big data analysis-কে S3 থেকে data read করতে হবে এবং output আবার S3-এ রাখতে হবে, যাতে আপনার customer-দের কাছে পাঠানো যায়। Big Data analysis চালাতে আপনি কোন technology recommend করবেন?

Correct: C. Why it is right

Nijer lekha Spark job, S3 theke pore S3 e output: EMR Hadoop / Spark cluster banay ar Spark bundled thake (PDF p. 543). Course er answer EMR.

Note: Glue o serverless Spark ETL job chalay (S6-Q28 e Glue-o correct), kintu ei single-answer proshne key EMR.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Redshift SQL data warehouse; nijer Spark job chalay na.
  • B. Proshner answer key Glue ke ETL tool dhore (big data analysis na); aaj Glue Spark job chalate pare, kintu course er Spark answer EMR.
  • D. Athena serverless SQL on S3; Spark code chalay na.

Keyword: Spark job + big data analysis S3 → S3 → EMR

Original explanation (English)

Athena is serverless SQL, Redshift is SQL, Glue is for ETL, not Big Data Analysis. EMR is for launching Hadoop / Spark clusters and is the right answer here

22·10S6-Q3Stephane set 6 · Q3Design Resilient Architectures

A Big Data analytics company is using a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances to ingest Internet-of-Things (IoT) data from various data sources. The data is in JSON format and ingestion rates can be as high as 1 MB/s. When an EC2 instance is restarted, the in-flight data is lost. The analytics team at the company wants to query ingested data in near-real-time.

Which of the following solutions provides near-real-time data querying that is scalable with minimal data loss?

একটি Big Data analytics company বিভিন্ন data source থেকে Internet-of-Things (IoT) data ingest করতে Amazon EC2 instance-এর একটি fleet ব্যবহার করছে। data JSON format-এ এবং ingestion rate 1 MB/s পর্যন্ত হতে পারে। কোনো EC2 instance restart হলে in-flight data হারিয়ে যায়। company-র analytics team ingest করা data near-real-time-এ query করতে চায়।

নিচের কোন solution ন্যূনতম data loss-সহ scalable near-real-time data querying দেয়?

Renamed: Kinesis Data Firehose -> Amazon Data Firehose; Kinesis Data Analytics -> Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (the answer is the same).

Correct: C. Why it is right

EC2 te ingest korle restart e in-flight data harai. Firehose fully managed, auto scale (shard provision lage na), data sorasori Redshift e load kore (S3 e likhe COPY diye) (PDF p. 537). Redshift e SQL diye near-real-time query.

Tai scalable + minimal data loss + near-real-time query = Firehose → Redshift.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Instance store ephemeral; instance stop / fail e data harai, minimal data loss bhange.
  • B. EBS + ElastiCache Redis: ElastiCache cache, query store na; Redis channel subscribe data query er solution na.
  • D. KDS te shard manage lage, ar KDS + Kinesis Data Analytics (ekhon Managed Flink) data long-term store kore na, warehouse er moto query o na.

Keyword: near-real-time querying + scalable + minimal data loss → Firehose → Redshift

Original explanation (English)

Correct option:

Capture data in Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon Redshift as the destination. Use Amazon Redshift to query the data - Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is the easiest way to reliably load streaming data into data lakes, data stores, and analytics services. It can capture, transform, and deliver streaming data to Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Elasticsearch Service, generic HTTP endpoints, and service providers like Datadog, New Relic, MongoDB, and Splunk.

Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is the easiest way to capture, transform, and load streaming data into Redshift for near real-time analytics. It is also an auto-scaling solution as there is no need to provision any shards like Kinesis Data Streams.

Redshift allows you to run complex analytic queries against petabytes of structured data, using sophisticated query optimization, columnar storage on high-performance local disks, and massively parallel query execution. Most results come back in seconds.

Incorrect options:

Capture data in an EC2 instance store and then publish this data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon S3 as the destination. Use Amazon Athena to query the data - Instance store is a temporary storage available on Amazon EC2 instances. Data in the instance store is lost if the instance is rebooted. Hence, this cannot be the option for the current use case.

Capture data in an EBS volume and then publish this data to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Subscribe to the Redis channel to query the data - EBS volumes cannot be used to store high volume data. EBS can be used to store cache data if a database is hosted on an EC2 instance. However, EBS cannot be used in place of a database. ElastiCache is a caching service. It is not relevant to the given use case.

Capture data in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query and analyze this streaming data in real-time - For Kinesis Data Streams, you have to manually allocate the shards for scaling the data ingestion process. Kinesis Data Streams (KDS) and Kinesis Data Analytics are for real-time processing of data and cannot provide long-term storage of data unlike a database or a data warehouse. So, this option is not right for the current use case.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/redshift/features/

https://aws.amazon.com/kinesis/data-firehose/faqs/

https://aws.amazon.com/kinesis/data-analytics/faqs/

https://aws.amazon.com/kinesis/data-streams/faqs/

References: https://aws.amazon.com/redshift/features/ · https://aws.amazon.com/kinesis/data-firehose/faqs/ · https://aws.amazon.com/kinesis/data-analytics/faqs/ · https://aws.amazon.com/kinesis/data-streams/faqs/

22·11S6-Q26Stephane set 6 · Q26Design Cost-Optimized Architectures

Your company has created a data warehouse using Redshift that is used to analyze data from Amazon S3. From the usage pattern, you have detected that after 30 days, the data is rarely queried in Redshift and it's not "hot data" anymore. You would like to preserve the SQL querying capability on your data and get the queries started immediately. Also, you want to adopt a pricing model that allows you to save the maximum amount of cost on Redshift.

What do you recommend? (Select two)

আপনার company Redshift ব্যবহার করে একটি data warehouse তৈরি করেছে, যা Amazon S3-এর data analyze করতে ব্যবহৃত হয়। usage pattern থেকে আপনি দেখেছেন যে 30 দিন পরে Redshift-এ data খুব কমই query করা হয় এবং এটি আর "hot data" নয়। আপনি আপনার data-র ওপর SQL querying capability রাখতে চান এবং query সাথে সাথে শুরু হোক তা চান। এছাড়া আপনি এমন একটি pricing model গ্রহণ করতে চান, যা আপনাকে Redshift-এ সর্বোচ্চ পরিমাণ cost বাঁচাতে দেয়।

আপনি কী recommend করবেন? (2টি বেছে নিন) (Select two)

Choose 2 answers

Correct: D, E. Why it is right

  • S3 Standard-IA (30 din por): kom access er data, kintu dorkar hole rapid access; storage price kom (minimum 30 din storage charge).
  • Athena: S3 er cold data te serverless SQL, query sathe sathe, pay per query (PDF p. 531).

Redshift e shudhu hot data rekhe cost bachao, SQL querying thake.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Redshift er storage e S3 er moto tier / storage class nai; ei option possible na.
  • B. Choto Redshift cluster o cluster cost; data barle storage cost barte thakbe.
  • C. S3 Glacier e data query korar age restore lage; immediate SQL query hobe na.

Keyword: not hot data after 30 days + SQL, queries started immediately + save cost → S3 Standard-IA + Athena

Original explanation (English)

Correct options:

Move the data to S3 Standard IA after 30 days - S3 Standard-IA is for data that is accessed less frequently but requires rapid access when needed. S3 Standard-IA offers high durability, high throughput, and low latency of S3 Standard, with a low per GB storage price and per GB retrieval fee. This combination of low cost and high performance makes S3 Standard-IA ideal for long-term storage, backups, and as a data store for disaster recovery files. The minimum storage duration charge is 30 days.

Analyze the cold data with Athena - Amazon Athena is an interactive query service that makes it easy to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. Athena is serverless, so there is no infrastructure to set up or manage, and customers pay only for the queries they run. You can use Athena to process logs, perform ad-hoc analysis, and run interactive queries.

Moving the data to S3 glacier will prevent us from being able to query it. Therefore, we should migrate the data to S3 Standard IA and use Athena to analyze the cold data.

Incorrect options:

Migrate the Redshift underlying storage to S3 IA - Amazon Redshift is a fully-managed petabyte-scale cloud-based data warehouse product designed for large scale data set storage and analysis. An Amazon Redshift data warehouse is a collection of computing resources called nodes, which are organized into a group called a cluster. Each cluster runs an Amazon Redshift engine and contains one or more databases. An Amazon Redshift cluster consists of nodes. Each cluster has a leader node and one or more compute nodes. The leader node receives queries from client applications, parses the queries, and develops query execution plans. The leader node then coordinates the parallel execution of these plans with the compute nodes and aggregates the intermediate results from these nodes. It then finally returns the results to the client applications.

Redshift's internal storage does not have "tiers" of storage classes like Amazon S3, so this option is also ruled out.

Create a smaller Redshift Cluster with the cold data - Creating a smaller cluster with the cold data would not decrease the storage cost of Redshift, which will only increase with time as we keep on creating data. Therefore this option is ruled out.

Move the data to S3 Glacier after 30 days - Amazon S3 Glacier and S3 Glacier Deep Archive are secure, durable, and extremely low-cost Amazon S3 cloud storage classes for data archiving and long-term backup. They are designed to deliver 99.999999999% durability, and provide comprehensive security and compliance capabilities that can help meet even the most stringent regulatory requirements.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/athena/

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/working-with-clusters.html

The engineering team at a company wants to create a daily big data analysis job leveraging Spark for analyzing online/offline sales and customer loyalty data to create customized reports on a client-by-client basis. The big data analysis job needs to read the data from Amazon S3 and output it back to S3.

Which technology do you recommend to run the Big Data analysis job? (Select two)

একটি company-র engineering team Spark ব্যবহার করে একটি দৈনিক big data analysis job তৈরি করতে চায়, যা online/offline sales ও customer loyalty data analyze করে client-by-client ভিত্তিতে customized report তৈরি করবে। big data analysis job-কে Amazon S3 থেকে data read করতে হবে এবং output আবার S3-এ রাখতে হবে।

Big Data analysis job চালাতে আপনি কোন technology recommend করবেন? (2টি বেছে নিন) (Select two)

Choose 2 answers

Correct: B, C. Why it is right

  • Amazon EMR: managed Hadoop / Spark cluster; S3 theke pore S3 e lekhe; short job er jonno cluster spin up / down (transient) (PDF p. 543-544).
  • AWS Glue: serverless Spark-based ETL; Glue job S3 theke pore, transform kore, S3 e lekhe (PDF p. 548).

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Redshift SQL data warehouse; Spark job chalanor platform na.
  • D. Athena serverless SQL query engine; Spark job chalay na.
  • E. AWS Batch EC2 te batch job schedule kore, kintu managed Spark platform na; Spark cluster nije setup korte hobe.

Keyword: daily big data job leveraging Spark, S3 → S3 (select two) → EMR + Glue

Original explanation (English)

Correct option:

Amazon EMR - Amazon EMR is the industry-leading cloud big data platform for processing vast amounts of data using open source tools such as Apache Spark, Apache Hive, Apache HBase, Apache Flink, Apache Hudi, and Presto. With EMR you can run Petabyte-scale analysis at less than half of the cost of traditional on-premises solutions and over 3x faster than standard Apache Spark. EMR is used for launching Hadoop / Spark clusters. For short-running jobs, you can spin up and spin down clusters and pay per second for the instances used. For long-running workloads, you can create highly available clusters that automatically scale to meet demand. Amazon EMR uses Hadoop, an open-source framework, to distribute your data and processing across a resizable cluster of Amazon EC2 instances.

AWS Glue - AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, and load (ETL) service that makes it easy for customers to prepare and load their data for analytics. AWS Glue job is meant to be used for batch ETL data processing. AWS Glue ETL jobs can use Amazon S3, data stores in a VPC, or on-premises JDBC data stores as a source. AWS Glue jobs extract data, transform it, and load the resulting data back to S3, data stores in a VPC, or on-premises JDBC data stores as a target.

Incorrect options:

Amazon Redshift - Amazon Redshift is a fully-managed petabyte-scale cloud-based data warehouse product designed for large scale data set storage and analysis. An Amazon Redshift data warehouse is a collection of computing resources called nodes, which are organized into a group called a cluster. Each cluster runs an Amazon Redshift engine and contains one or more databases. An Amazon Redshift cluster consists of nodes. Each cluster has a leader node and one or more compute nodes. The leader node receives queries from client applications, parses the queries, and develops query execution plans. The leader node then coordinates the parallel execution of these plans with the compute nodes and aggregates the intermediate results from these nodes. It then finally returns the results to the client applications.

Amazon Athena - Amazon Athena is an interactive query service that makes it easy to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. Athena is serverless, so there is no infrastructure to set up or manage, and customers pay only for the queries they run. You can use Athena to process logs, perform ad-hoc analysis, and run interactive queries.

AWS Batch AWS Batch can be used to plan, schedule, and execute your batch computing workloads on Amazon EC2 Instances. AWS Batch dynamically provisions the optimal quantity and type of compute resources (e.g., CPU or memory optimized compute resources) based on the volume and specific resource requirements of the batch jobs submitted.

A Big Data company wants to optimize its daily Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) process that migrates and transforms data from its S3 based data lake to a Redshift cluster. The team wants to manage this daily job in a serverless environment.

Which AWS service is the best fit to manage this process without the need to configure or manage the underlying compute resources?

একটি Big Data company তাদের দৈনিক Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) process optimize করতে চায়, যা তাদের S3-ভিত্তিক data lake থেকে একটি Redshift cluster-এ data migrate ও transform করে। team এই দৈনিক job-টি একটি serverless environment-এ manage করতে চায়।

underlying compute resource configure বা manage করার প্রয়োজন ছাড়াই এই process manage করতে কোন AWS service সবচেয়ে উপযুক্ত (best fit)?

Correct: C. Why it is right

AWS Glue serverless Apache Spark environment e managed ETL chalay: S3 data lake theke data extract, transform kore Redshift e load (PDF p. 548). Compute provision / configure / scale Glue nije kore, tumi shudhu job er taka dao.

Why the other options are wrong

  • A. Data Pipeline EC2 / EMR resource launch kore tomar account e; serverless na. Ar eta ekhon notun customer der jonno bondho (maintenance mode).
  • B. EMR EC2 cluster e chole, node manage korte hoy; "without managing compute" bhange.
  • D. DMS database migration / replication er jonno; S3 data lake → Redshift er daily ETL transform er tool na.

Keyword: daily ETL S3 → Redshift + serverless, no compute to manage → AWS Glue

Original explanation (English)

Correct option:

AWS Glue - AWS Glue provides a managed ETL service that runs on a serverless Apache Spark environment. This allows you to focus on your ETL job and not worry about configuring and managing the underlying compute resources. AWS Glue takes a data-first approach and allows you to focus on the data properties and data manipulation to transform the data to a form where you can derive business insights. It provides an integrated data catalog that makes metadata available for ETL as well as querying via Amazon Athena and Amazon Redshift Spectrum.

Create a unified catalog to find data across multiple data stores using Glue: via - https://aws.amazon.com/glue/

AWS Glue automates much of the effort required for data integration. AWS Glue crawls your data sources, identifies data formats, and suggests schemas to store your data. It automatically generates the code to run your data transformations and loading processes. You can use AWS Glue to easily run and manage thousands of ETL jobs or to combine and replicate data across multiple data stores using SQL.

AWS Glue runs in a serverless environment. There is no infrastructure to manage, and AWS Glue provisions, configures, and scales the resources required to run your data integration jobs. You pay only for the resources your jobs use while running.

AWS Glue is the right fit since the company is looking at a managed ETL service without having the overhead of configuring, maintaining, or managing any servers.

[chobi: original link, ekhon na-o thakte pare] via - https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/load-data-from-amazon-s3-to-amazon-redshift-using-aws-glue.html

Incorrect options:

AWS Data Pipeline - AWS Data Pipeline provides a managed orchestration service that gives you greater flexibility in terms of the execution environment, access and control over the compute resources that run your code, as well as the code itself that does data processing. AWS Data Pipeline launches compute resources in your account allowing you direct access to the Amazon EC2 instances or Amazon EMR clusters. As this option provides access to the underlying EC2 instances so it's not a serverless solution. Therefore this option is incorrect for the given use case.

Amazon EMR - EMR is a web service to easily and cost-effectively process vast amounts of data. EMR utilizes a hosted Hadoop framework running on the web-scale infrastructure of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). As this option provides access to the underlying EC2 instances so it's not a serverless solution. Therefore this option is incorrect for the given use case.

AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) - AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) helps you migrate databases to AWS easily and securely. For use cases that require a database migration from on-premises to AWS or database replication between on-premises sources and sources on AWS, AWS recommends you use AWS DMS. Once your data is in AWS, you can use AWS Glue to move, combine, replicate, and transform data from your data source into another database or data warehouse, such as Amazon Redshift. As the use-case talks about data migration and transformation between AWS services, so AWS Glue is a better fit than DMS.
